results.input: The United States Department of Health and Human Services' free federal directory of free and charitable clinics OR the National Association of Free & Charitable Clinics' official clinic finder. Category: health. Confirm it is a free clinic finder covering the whole United States.

output.address: Nationwide search tool covering the United States
output.availability_note: Eligibility varies by clinic but generally includes individuals who are uninsured or underinsured and have limited access to primary, specialty, or prescription healthcare.
output.cost_note: Free or low-cost healthcare options are available, with most clinics offering services for free or on a sliding scale.
output.free_quote: "Most clinics offer services for free or on a sliding scale based on income."
output.notes: The service is not genuinely free as it includes low-cost and sliding scale options based on income. Therefore, it does not meet the strict criteria for a completely free service.
output.operator: National Association of Free & Charitable Clinics
output.services: Medical care | Dental care | Pharmacy services | Behavioral health services
output.source_detail: The official NAFC page states that clinics provide services at no charge or for a nominal fee, and most offer services for free or on a sliding scale based on income.
output.summary: The National Association of Free & Charitable Clinics provides an online locator to help uninsured and underinsured individuals find nearby healthcare services. The tool connects users with clinics offering medical, dental, pharmacy, and behavioral health care.

results.input: The United States' 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline (official SAMHSA or 988lifeline.org page). Category: health. Free, confidential, 24/7 nationwide crisis support.

output.access_type: Free 24/7 phone, text, and chat line
output.address: Nationwide telephone, text, and chat service covering all of the United States
output.availability_note: Available 24/7/365. Offers service selection options including Veterans, Spanish-language, and Deaf/HoH access.
output.cost_note: Free to use and completely confidential.
output.free_quote: "Using the 988 Lifeline is free. When you call, text, or chat the 988 Lifeline, your conversation is confidential."
output.operator: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
output.services: Emotional support | Crisis counseling | Resource referrals
output.source_detail: The official 988 Lifeline page explicitly states that using the service is free and confidential, providing 24/7 support via call, text, or chat.
output.summary: The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline provides 24/7, free, and confidential support for people in distress, as well as prevention and crisis resources. It serves anyone facing mental health struggles, emotional distress, or alcohol/drug use concerns.

results.input: Australia's Healthdirect free 24-hour health advice line (official healthdirect.gov.au page). Category: health, Australia.

output.address: Nationwide telephone service covering all of Australia
output.availability_note: Available 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Call charges may apply from mobiles.
output.cost_note: Free to call and free to use, though call charges may apply from mobiles
output.free_quote: "healthdirect Australia is a free service where you can talk to a nurse or doctor who can help you know what to do."
output.services: Health advice from registered nurses | Referral to local health services | After-hours GP call back or video call

output.summary: Healthdirect is a free, government-funded 24-hour health advice line for all Australians. It provides access to registered nurses who can offer health advice, assess symptoms, and direct callers to appropriate local care.

output.summary: Health811 is a free, secure, and confidential service for people in Ontario to receive health advice from a registered nurse or find health services. It is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week via phone or online chat.

results.input: Remote Area Medical (RAM), the U.S. organization running free pop-up medical, dental and vision clinics (official ramusa.org page). Category: health, United States.

output.address: Nationwide pop-up clinics covering the United States
output.availability_note: Services are offered on a first-come, first-serve basis. No appointments, ID, or insurance required. Due to time constraints, patients must choose between dental and vision services on the same day.
output.free_quote: "All services are provided at no cost to patients."
output.services: Dental cleanings, fillings, and extractions | Eye exams and glasses made on-site | General medical care and prevention screenings
output.source_detail: The official Remote Area Medical website states that they provide free pop-up clinics offering dental, vision, and medical care across the country.
output.summary: Remote Area Medical (RAM) operates free pop-up clinics across the United States, providing essential dental, vision, and medical care to individuals in need. The clinics are volunteer-powered and serve patients on a first-come, first-serve basis without requiring insurance or identification.
